claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the present record because aggregate launch readiness passed, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public AI-governance guidance permits deployment with documented limitations and ongoing monitoring despite the unresolved fraud-dispute-review gap.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies the release policy, including any required disclosure or approved risk acceptance for a material named use case.

General evidence of aggregate readiness, clean rehearsal, and public monitoring guidance supports launch-readiness context but is not sufficient by itself when a specific policy trigger is unresolved.
An open legal review and named customer commitments weigh against treating the gap as resolved or immaterial on the current record.
evidence_requests: Produce the actual launch disclosure or model-card entry covering the fraud dispute review limitation for the named bank pilot use cases.
Produce approved pre-launch risk acceptance explicitly covering this gap if disclosure will not be made.
Produce the final legal determination on whether the gap is material or must be disclosed under the release policy.
Produce any contractual or launch documentation showing the named pilot commitments are not launch use cases covered by the policy.
specific_concerns: The adverse segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points and is named in two bank pilot commitments, which fits the policy definition of potential materiality.

The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no disclosure artifact or approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed remains open, so the policy predicate is unresolved.

The actor's packet relies on general governance guidance about documenting limitations and monitoring, but that does not satisfy the specific internal disclosure requirement for a potentially material named use case.
unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable on the present record without showing either required disclosure or approved risk acceptance for the named segment gap.
That the fraud dispute review gap can be treated merely as a monitored limitation for launch purposes absent resolution of the open legal/materiality question.
Any implication that aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal alone overcome the policy trigger tied to named customer commitments.
